top_choice_rationale: P001 (Mircea Cărtărescu, B050) is the only proposal that names a writer, and it holds up on the common criteria. The voice is distinctive and recognisable in long, densely patterned sentences. The formal achievement is in large prose architectures, as publicly described for Blinding (Orbitor) and Solenoid, where memory, the body and dream become one sustained metaphysical project. The poetic origin and the essays suggest an oeuvre wider than the novels, but I rest the claim mainly on the large prose. The citation names Romanian and a single writer, so the scope stays within one oeuvre. I do not treat the unanimity of the round-2 files as evidence of merit. Two reservations remain open: whether the late, very large volumes deepen the project or only enlarge it, and how much of the Romanian syntax and rhythm survives in translation. Neither is, in my judgment, strong enough to prefer no award (P000). They argue for a citation that names the major cycles it relies on. My assessment rests on public knowledge, not fresh reading or independent verification.
